title: Claim Bucket Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Claim Verification
Source Discovery
Fact-Verified Poster
Sorting Quiz
Category Bucket
description: Drag twelve invented evidence records, each a planned claim with a source type and quoted passage, into the VERIFIED, DIRECTIONAL, QUALITATIVE-ONLY and REJECTED buckets; feedback names the deciding rule and a summary lists misses by pattern.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Classifying evidence for poster claims into the four verification buckets
learningObjectives: The learner will classify evidence records for a planned claim as VERIFIED, DIRECTIONAL, QUALITATIVE-ONLY or REJECTED, and will justify each choice from the quoted passage and the source type.
prerequisites: Finding and Verifying Sources section of Chapter 11
The difference between a primary study and a review or meta-analysis

dependencies: data.json (twelve practice records, loaded with loadJSON)

accessibility.notes: Keys 1-4 sort the card without dragging; describe() reports each result and its rule

controls.label: Evidence record card
controls.purpose: Drag into a bucket to classify the record

controls.label: VERIFIED, DIRECTIONAL, QUALITATIVE-ONLY, REJECTED
controls.purpose: The four verification buckets; keys 1-4 also sort

controls.label: Show rule
controls.purpose: Reveal the deciding question; the record then scores 5 instead of 10

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification with immediate rule-based feedback and a pattern summary
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Drag-to-bucket sorting quiz with hint penalty
keyQuestions: Can a meta-analysis ever VERIFY a number?
Why can a claim with no number not be VERIFIED?
Does a peer-reviewed source always support the claim it is cited for?
commonMisconceptions: Any number from a meta-analysis is VERIFIED
The top of a reported range is the result
A peer-reviewed source always supports the claim
A missing number means the claim must be rejected
assessmentOpportunities: Score out of 120 with rules shown
